headline: REA Maps the Black Box
lede: REA gives coding agents a disciplined route into binaries, firmware, applications, and other artifacts without source access. Its local workflows connect established reverse-engineering tools to evidence-backed conclusions—and a daily surge of 41,034 stars signals immediate demand.

headline: Claude Code Opens Its Plugin Exchange
lede: Anthropic’s official marketplace turns Claude Code extensions into a structured, installable ecosystem. Standard manifests, MCP integration, bundled skills, and stable naming give agent builders a clear framework for extending the coding environment without losing control of the catalog.

headline: A Field Guide for AI Scientists
lede: Scientific Agent Skills assembles 163 validated capabilities across more than 100 scientific databases. The collection gives researchers a portable, documented way to connect agents with bioinformatics, drug discovery, physics, and geospatial workflows while keeping local execution in reach.

headline: Caveman Cuts the Agent Chatter
lede: Caveman puts a local proxy between coding agents and the noisy data they process, compressing logs, JSON, and code before they consume another token. Reversible SQLite backups and support for more than 30 tools make the approach practical: less throat-clearing, lower bills, recoverable context.

headline: Voice Production Moves Back On Device
lede: VoiceStudio brings cloning, dubbing, synthesis, and audiobook production onto the desktop instead of sending projects to a cloud service. With hundreds of languages, swappable engines, and hardware acceleration for CUDA, Apple Silicon, and ROCm, the pipeline keeps both models and source material local.

headline: Superpowers Gives Coding Agents a Process
lede: Superpowers replaces the rush from prompt to patch with a measured sequence: discover requirements, validate a design, plan the work, then build and test in small steps. Worktrees, TDD, review, and subagents form a repeatable construction plan for teams that want autonomy without abandoning engineering discipline.

headline: Ruflo Builds a Company of Agents
lede: Ruflo provides the execution layer for multi-agent engineering, coordinating specialized workers, persistent memory, plugins, and cross-machine communication. Its Rust engine, optional vector databases, and background services aim at the operational problem behind autonomous software: state, routing, security, and scale.

headline: Context Mode Moves Work Outside the Window
lede: Context Mode routes bulky tool output into sandboxed execution, returning findings instead of flooding the model with raw data. SQLite persistence, full-text retrieval, and integrations across 17 clients turn long coding sessions into a smaller, searchable stream of decisions and results.

headline: Ghidra Opens the Binary Underneath
lede: Ghidra remains a formidable workbench for disassembly, decompilation, graphing, and scripting across platforms and processor families. Its Java and Python extensibility, automation paths, and collaborative project model give analysts a durable foundation for examining software at the instruction level.

headline: ECC Puts Agent Workflows Under Review
lede: ECC turns coding assistants into a governed loop of planning, testing, implementation, review, verification, and memory. Its AgentShield layer scans prompts, hooks, MCP settings, permissions, secrets, and agent files—treating the expanding automation surface as something to inspect before it ships.
